facts.subject: Folk of the Fells
facts.statement: Strong, not tall, black-haired, blue- or grey-eyed, cheerful and talkative; women comely and kind but refusing strangers' caresses.

refs.q: strong men, but not high of stature, black-haired, with blue or grey eyes, cheerful of countenance, and of many words

facts.subject: Folk of the Fells
facts.statement: They keep no thralls: adult captives are sold, killed or ransomed; captured children are sometimes adopted.

refs.q: when they took men and women, as oft they did, they always sold them for what they would bring to the plain-dwellers; or else slew them, or held them to ransom, but never brought them home to their stead

facts.subject: Folk of the Fells
facts.statement: Their gods are their forefathers; adopted children are made kin with prayers and worship.

refs.q: made them very children of their Folk with many uncouth prayers and worship of their Gods, who were indeed, as they deemed, but forefathers of the Folk

facts.subject: Folk of the Fells
facts.statement: They hunt hart, boar and wild bulls in the mountains.

refs.q: they showed the wayfarers their manner of hunting, both of the hart and the boar, and of wild bulls also

facts.subject: (unnamed) town of the Folk of the Fells
facts.statement: Its defence is concealment and defensible approaches.

ledger.summary: Two days on they reach the Folk of the Fells' town in a hidden, defensible mountain valley: plain houses, the chief one like a great abbey barn where most people gather. The people are strong but not tall, black-haired, blue- or grey-eyed, cheerful and talkative; the women are comely and kind but allow no caresses from strangers. They keep no thralls: captives are sold, killed or ransomed, but captured children may be adopted with prayers to their gods, who are their forefathers. They feast the travellers three days and hunt hart, boar and wild bulls; Ralph excels and is thought a god. On the fourth day the chief escorts them by other ways, avoiding the Mid-Mountain House, down to the plain, where the Goldburg men take their wages and return with the wild men, who weep at parting.
ledger.geography_notes: Two days' travel from the pass wood to a fair valley in the mountains holding the Folk of the Fells' town: hard to find and easily defended. From there, other ways (avoiding the Mid-Mountain House) lead down to the plain.
